newsitem.title: USA: US awards $38 million for 'smart' traffic projects.
newsitem.headline: US awards $38 million for 'smart' traffic projects.

text.p: Awards of $38.7 million were announced for four metropolitan areas to help develop "smart" methods to cut traffic congestion and speed travel times, the Transportation Department announed on Thursday.

It said the "intelligent infrastructure" demonstration projects would include electronic traffic management, automated fare payment and toll collection and freeway and grade-crossing integration to merge an area's road and transit flows into a single, smooth-moving transportation system.

Transportation Secretary Federico Pena presented the first grant of $7.5 million to Phoenix. He said other grants would go to San Antonio, $7.1 million; Seattle, $13.7 million; and the New York, New Jersey, Connecticut region, $10.4 million.

He said the programs were designed to cut the daily travel time of people in congested areas by 15 percent over the next two years, adding that the new technology can keep the flow of people and goods moving more smoothly, safely and with less impact on the environment.
